adjudicated_by: Architect (in-session adjudicator, same authoring session: not independent of it; independence is asserted, not enforced)
adjudication_rationale: Public XNU xnu-12377.1.9 was read, not reproduced and not the kernel on this host: proc_pidinfo -> proc_find -> proc_ref_wait_for_exec (kern_proc.c:827-885, THREAD_UNINT, no timeout), but the wait bits are set and cleared entirely inside proc_exec_switch_task (kern_exec.c:5143/5145 set, :5272-5273 clear), called at :4454 and :5476 only AFTER exec_activate_image (:4424/:5460) has loaded the image. So the reported trigger (exec of a binary on an unresponsive network mount) does not hold the window; between set and clear there is only in-memory bookkeeping. Residual: proc_refdrain_will_exec waits for outstanding references, so a third thread holding a reference and itself blocked could stall it. agents/core/src/agent.cpp:4180 thread_pool_.reset() is an unbounded join for every plugin execute(), so the root cause is agent-core, and bounded_call from plugin text is forbidden by the tree (agents/core/include/yuzu/agent/passwd_lookup.hpp:7-25: a detached thread in a dlclose-able plugin is a use-after-unload). Default-off, single-target, AdminOrApproval plugin.

summary: Derived HIGH by I5 clause (c) (reconnect wedge); sre native MEDIUM. De-escalated by the Architect to a text fix plus the existing core follow-up, no bounded_call in this PR. adjudicated_by: Architect (in-session adjudicator, same authoring session: not independent of it; independence is asserted, not enforced)
adjudication_rationale: Accepted residual. The guard is a string compare (legs.hpp:478) over sec*1e6+usec (parsers.hpp mac_start_number); XNU kern_fork.c:1131 stamps p_start once at fork from the wall clock and :1126-1127 copies it across exec, so a collision on a recycled pid needs all three: pid recycled, wall clock stepped back past the old start, new start equal to the microsecond. A clock-free identity exists in the kernel (p_uniqueid, kern_fork.c:980) but the public SDK header sys/proc_info.h on this host exposes neither its flavour nor its struct, so it is not reachable through public libproc. Linux ships a 10 ms bucket for the same property.
trigger: pid recycled AND wall clock stepped back past the old start AND new p_start equal to the old one to the microsecond: the token matches and the guard passes for a different process
classification_rationale: README caveat 3 read as if a clock step alone defeats the guard; three conditions are needed
summary: Table band HIGH (I3/E5), native NICE; accepted as a residual with a README wording fix (all three conditions named, and 'public libproc exposes no clock-free identity', not 'no better source exists'). No code change. README fix in a0c145d554 (kept through f2f039cc09).
